overviewParagraphs: Dragon Golf Links near Hai Phong is one of the most authentic links-style golf experiences in Northern Vietnam. Positioned directly on the coast with the sea encroaching on multiple holes, the layout offers a wind-driven challenge that demands the full repertoire of creative shot-making that defines genuine links play.

Firm and fast playing conditions reward the low-running approach, and the natural coastal bunkering provides both visual drama and tactical consequence. The course changes character completely depending on wind direction, ensuring every visit feels like a fresh challenge even for returning players.

An excellent choice for the discerning golfer who wants a pure links experience in the north of Vietnam. Its coastal character, accessibility from Hanoi, and tactical depth make Dragon Golf Links a standout addition to any extended northern Vietnam golf itinerary.

curatorBriefHtml: Dragon Golf Links at Dragon Ocean Do Son (Hai Phong) is one of Northern Vietnam’s boldest recent openings — a Greg Norman-designed 27-hole coastal links built on reclaimed peninsula land jutting directly into the Gulf of Tonkin. Virtually every hole plays in full view of the sea with minimal tree cover, putting wind management and low, controlled ball flights at the center of your round.

Positioned roughly 90 minutes from Hanoi via the smooth Hanoi–Hai Phong Expressway and only 30 minutes from Cat Bi International Airport (HPH), Dragon Golf Links is rapidly reshaping Northern Vietnam golf circuits. Its firm coastal turf, sprawling waste bunkers, and exposed sea-edge closing holes deliver a links aesthetic previously found only on Vietnam’s Central Coast at Hoiana Shores.

Because ocean gusts pick up noticeably after midday on the Do Son peninsula, AGS targets morning tee times between 07:30 and 09:00 AM and pairs Dragon Golf Links with FLC Ha Long Bay or Silk Path Dong Trieu for an unforgettable northeast coast swing.

scorecard.verdict: Constructed on reclaimed land jutting directly into the Gulf of Tonkin, Dragon Golf Links exposes players to authentic coastal gale conditions and scenic open-water panoramas on nearly every hole.

faqs.q: How does Dragon Golf Links compare to Vietnam's other Greg Norman courses?
faqs.a: Compared with Norman’s dune-sculpted layout at The Bluffs Ho Tram or the coastal corridors at BRG Da Nang, Dragon Golf Links sits directly on a flat, wind-exposed sea peninsula in Hai Phong — making sea breeze strategy and bunker avoidance the defining test on nearly every hole.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Hanoi or Ha Long Bay to Dragon Golf Links?
faqs.a: Dragon Golf Links is approximately 90 to 100 minutes from central Hanoi via the modern Hanoi–Hai Phong Expressway, 30 minutes from Hai Phong’s Cat Bi Airport (HPH), and roughly 60 minutes from Ha Long Bay.

faqs.q: What wind and seasonal conditions should golfers expect at Do Son?
faqs.a: Wind is a daily factor year-round on the peninsula. October through April brings cooler, brisk northeast breezes (pack a windproof pullover in December–February), while spring and summer mornings offer calmer air before afternoon sea winds build.

faqs.q: Can Dragon Golf Links be combined with Ha Long Bay on a multi-day tour?
faqs.a: Yes — it pairs seamlessly with FLC Ha Long Bay and Silk Path Dong Trieu on a 4- to 6-day Northeast Vietnam circuit, or as a dramatic coastal finale to a Hanoi golf tour.
